text:
Jules H: FYI ran a focused AWQ bakeoff across FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ variants for the new chat-medium v2. Results look promising for AWQ latency/cost, but seeing intermittent serving instability when act-quant is enabled and group_size >= 64.
Priya K: Ugh. Can you paste the failure signature?
Jules H: gist of logs below. errors spike ~3-7% request-level timeouts and some token corruption (mismatched brackets).
Jules H: ```
[2026-03-15T16:12:11Z] serve: request id=bb3f latency=120ms model=chat-med-v2-awq group_size=64 act_quant=true state=OK
[2026-03-15T16:12:12Z] serve: request id=bb3f latency=130ms model=chat-med-v2-awq group_size=64 act_quant=true state=DECODE_ERROR token_seq=...
[2026-03-15T16:12:12Z] runtime: kv-cache-mismatch detected; fallback triggered to FP16 variant
[2026-03-15T16:12:13Z] metrics: flank_error_rate=0.035
```
Tom B: Is the instability correlated with throughput (QPS) or sequence length?
Jules H: Mostly at bursts - QPS > 250 on that pool. Also more frequent for longer context (seq > 1024). Short contexts are fine.
Olga P: Important: AWQ group-size combos were stable in offline eval - accuracy delta vs FP16 was +0.1% top-k but in-serve it flips occasionally. Could be a micro-batching interaction.
Priya K: Did you test with prefix/KV cache enabled vs disabled? That changed things before.
Jules H: Yes — reproduces with and without prefix cache, but error mode differs: with cache it's kv-cache-mismatch; without cache it's rare decode artifacts but fewer timeouts.
DevOps Sam: infra-bot shows a couple of infra events around the same time (node reclaim + small CPU steal). Attaching poller note.
infra-bot: [auto] node n-gpu-12 reported transient PCIe reset at 2026-03-15T16:11:59Z, pod redeployed.
Raj M: Could be sensitivity to kernel reorder or strided matmul quant rounding at certain batch alignments. We've seen similar with mixed act-quant + grouped matmul before.
Tom B: Quick hypothesis checklist: (1) alignment with CUDA kernel tiling for group_size 64, (2) act-quant saturation causing dynamic range edge cases, (3) batching * KV cache interplay.
Priya K: Agreed. Can we run an A/B where we vary only group_size (16/32/48/64/96) at stable low QPS and at high QPS? Need to separate load effect.
Jules H: On it. Kickoff plan: reproduce with synthetic traffic at target QPS, enable detailed trace for first 1% of requests (dump quant traces + kv-checksum), and run group sweep. Also will include GPTQ and FP8 baselines.
Olga P: Add eval probe that computes token-level BLEU/Rouge diffs vs FP16 baseline per request so we can correlate accuracy deltas with errors.
DevOps Sam: For the high-QPS test, I'll pin pod placement to avoid node reclaim and disable autoscaler.
Jules H: Early results from a small run: group_size 32 act_quant=true -> stable; 48 -> occasional decode drift (~0.8% bad token rate); 64 -> 3.5% bad token rate + timeouts; 96 -> catastrophic (10%+).
Raj M: That escalation profile screams quant rounding accumulation over grouped GEMMs. Suggest try act-clip thresholding (reduce dynamic range) and rerun.
Priya K: Also try hybrid: AWQ act_quant=false but weight-quant AWQ enabled (i.e., only weight quant). See if that isolates act path.
Jules H: Ran hybrid: act_quant=false group=64 -> stable, minor accuracy delta +0.2%. So act-quant path is the main culprit.
Tom B: Good find. Next: can we revert to per-token dequant (slower) and see if that eliminates drift? If yes, confirms accumulation error.
Jules H: Will test. If confirmed, mitigation options: (a) lower group_size to 32 for production, (b) enable act clipping, (c) fall back to hybrid AWQ (weights-only) for tail QPS, (d) upstream kernel fix.
Olga P: For rollout policy, recommend canary to 10% with auto-fallback to FP16 variant if flank_error_rate > 1% for 5m. Also add rollback trigger on token-level drift > 1% vs baseline.
DevOps Sam: Will add a temporary routing rule and SLO guardrail.
Jules H: Follow-ups: I'll open a PR with experiment configs (load profiles, traces, trace parser), and attach the sample traces. Assigning tracking ticket ML-5324.
Priya K: Thanks — please also log seed/version and exact awq binary hash.
Jules H: noted. Hash: awq-20260315-rc3.
Raj M: If anyone wants to reproduce quickly, here's a minimal runner snippet we used: ```python
# load AWQ model
model = load_model('chat-med-v2', quant='awq', act_quant=True, group_size=64)
runner = LocalRunner(model, qps=300, seq_len=1200)
runner.run(duration=600, traces=['kv-checksum','token-diff'])
```
Tom B: Great thread. Let's meet tomorrow 10am to review traces and pick mitigations. :calendar: :coffee:
